calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Flames’ net
calls.body: The Devils have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Flames near the bottom. Expect the Devils to spend more of the night in the Flames’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: New Jersey got the good looks
surprises.body: New Jersey’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Four points for Jack Hughes as the Devils beat the Flames
paras: Joel Hanley got the scoring started for the Flames late in the first. The second period was a wild one. Luke Hughes and Timo Meier scored just 12 seconds apart early in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Matt Coronato tied it 2-2 for Calgary midway through the period. Zach Whitecloud put the Flames up 3-2 late in the period, and that was all they would get. Jack Hughes tied it up for New Jersey early in the third, and Connor Brown put the Devils ahead for good with just under four minutes left. Luke Hughes scored his second of the night into the empty net with 11 seconds left. Jack Hughes finished with four points on a goal and three assists.

The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Devils win about seven in ten. Jake Allen made 26 saves for the Devils, and Devin Cooley stopped 29 of 33 at the other end. The Devils moved to 18-8-0, second in the Metropolitan, while the Flames fell to 11-14-2, slipping to sixth in the Pacific.
